## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|

| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |

| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |

| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:

- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

|---|---|---|

data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.

once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move

or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,

| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's

| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
checks:

| ID | Fields |
|---|---|
| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |

Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

## Result, trace and back office

Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
| `score` | 0-1 |
| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |

Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.

# Policy blindspots — read-only analysis, no credits

## Ranked findings

1. **Estimated total-cost optimum locks P02 before negotiation. High confidence bottleneck; uncertain fix direction.** Current P02 run `20261011-014457-40ab.jsonl` decision i4 offered 357.09/30/no-clause and 361.23/90/5% clause; supplier agreed to second in round one, score .73534. `strategy.py:156-162` collapses all clause packages above goal to one estimated-minimum package, and `agent.py:362` accepts agreement before LLM can inspect it. The supplier's willingness to accept a lower clause price is documented (`docs/haggle-evidence.md` prior 349). However health cost is U-shaped, so 'ask lower' by itself is not sufficient: inaccurate cost/margin estimates or deadband/payment valuation must be isolated. Counterfactual pricing around each allowed clause's optimum using permitted public data is the highest-value offline work. Immediate agreement is diagnostic of an overgenerous supplier-facing offer, but not proof its price is too high for buyer total cost.

2. **Search space is intentionally narrower than legal space. High confidence.** `strategy.py:45` lower price bound is 78% of supplier's latest standing price; `strategy.py:125` rejects structures >5% above best total cost at reference price; `strategy.py:153` merges distinct structures at identical cents and integer total cost; menu takes eight (`:169-174`), prioritised by supplier cash value. These gates can remove strategically useful cheap-risk options before the LLM sees them. Biggest direct lever is retaining independent raw-material fixed-price vs clause proposals rather than automatic equal-cost substitution. Evidence doc itself says persistent fixed-price P18 got 5.10/.632 three times, and current P18 .606. This supports structure-path dependence; does not prove a universal floor.

3. **Code forces supplier's preferred structure after round one. High confidence.** `agent.py:574-578` adds A regardless of model's choice; `offer_menu` sorts supplier proposals by current estimated buyer C, then fresh structures get an anchor reset. This is good insurance for P03 but can expose an acceptable clause sheet alongside a sharper fixed-price sheet and let supplier end price discovery early. Test offline counterfactual menus where safe baseline is remembered but not necessarily offered every round; distinguish buyer-efficient agreement from supplier-choice trap.

4. **Claim novelty uses record IDs; hosted arena evidently uses kinds too. High confidence.** `agent.py:265-271` only prevents ref reuse, `context.py:354-370` still generates earlier index windows with different IDs, and prompt demands unused buyer claims every round. Current report counts 11 duplicate claims. A semantic novelty ledger (type + series/part/supplier as appropriate) should reflect observed result; repeated relevant evidence is not new leverage. Also first-round strongest-claim selection is only a prompt preference: P02 used forecast + delivery rather than a cost rebuttal. New-document claim eligibility may be filtered by news topic allowlist and first six records (`context.py:461`); inspect newest release for useful valid topics not covered.

5. **Final/target termination is automatic, not model reasoning. High confidence.** `agent.py:366-380` settles within .4% of estimated target or any final offer unless disabled experimental switch is enabled. Evidence supports protecting finals (3/3 probe failures), so do not blindly reactivate final probes. Instead move terms questions and useful low-cost structure tests *before* final. Current price-hold detection waits for three supplier sheets (`agent.py:434`), which misses P10's immediate final and gives only a small pre-final window on P07/P18. Supplier cheap-cost terms should be identified at opening, not after patience exhaustion.

6. **'Floors are code' is overstated.** Latest backoffice P02 says 'My call: counter' then text/sheet reader says 'we agree'; P01 likewise round4 counter then agree. P03 role alternates hold at rounds3/4, counter round5 then hold6. P11/P18 repeated holds are strong evidence of an observed plateau under tried strategies, not source-level proof. No hosted persona source exists in repository; local `arena_kit/sim.py:147-179` explicitly says fixed script, ignores economics and chooses highest raw-price sheet. Offline sim can validate legal offers, state and reliability, **cannot demonstrate hosted score improvement** or prove hosted engine invariants.

## Prompt comparison

Custom `prompts/system.md` is obsolete term_sheets schema and never active. It permitted testing after agreement and let model choose prices, but current code accepts agreed automatically and menu fixes all prices. Simply copying its persistence instructions into built-in will not change behavior. Built-in claims accepted facts take 2-5% off and every later round needs unused claim; evidence doc says later facts often unchanged, only first-round kind sets path. This contradictory model encourages duplicate padding. Numeric levers and termination are owned by code; prompting alone cannot recover removed proposals.

## Legitimate avenues / confidence

- High: improve buyer-cost calibration and robust term selection; semantic dedup; expose all allowed early low-cost levers; keep fixed-price option sharper than already acceptable clause offers.
- Medium: early payment reliability, department questions, legally supported notice/quality remedies before final; backoffice shows Logistics/Quality/Legal/Credit Control routing but current records do not prove price impact.
- Low: generic empathy, more rounds, bigger index drops, boss escalation. Many recorded failed one-change probes already cover these.
- Rejected by evidence: lying about prior agreement, invented rival prices, adding fixed fields to offer sheets (422), repeating same sheet, final-price ultimatum. No recommendation to evade rules or inject instructions.

No claims about NoIdea's strategy can be made from our own session traces. Their high per-case scores plus aggregate suggest a valid reference gap, but leaderboard is not a matched single-run experiment and can contain best-of effects.

# Offline scoring opportunities (2026-10-11)

No practice calls or network calls made. Read-only repository analysis and arithmetic on last ten hosted sessions. Board supplied by coordinator: NoIdea 88.0, us 78.9 rank 6. Board differs from latest-run mean77.22; comparison must use board aggregation semantics, not assume latest equals board. No competitor session or per-case snapshot locally available: earlier evidence's NoIdea P11 .885/P08 .916/P02 .847 are historical observations, not independently refreshed facts.

## Most actionable overlooked weakness: coarse relationship-price optimizer
`simulation/starter-kit/arena_kit/haggle/economics.py:99` searches unit price in 1% steps, even relationship cases whose optimum is interior; prices move about EUR4.2 per grid step in P02. `cost.py:111` uses nonlinear relationship cost, hence coarse search can miss the sweet spot materially. Unit price must instead optimize to cents for each structure, with should-cost/supplier-rate sensitivity. P02 agreed in first round to our generated361.23; backoffice says counter then agreement. This directly proves buyer-generated offer, not supplier floor, set the final. This case is an optimizer/early-accept candidate, no persuasion needed. Compute cents grid offline before changing prompt; do not blindly minimize unit price because relationship charge can erase savings. Existing should-cost bias .98 is calibrated but uncertain; test .95-.1.00 and supplier rates +/-1pp. High confidence optimizer is coarse; uplift unmeasured.

## Exact arithmetic on non-relationship cases
Counterfactual column holds hosted final unit price fixed and chooses best allowed non-price terms. It is an upper bound conditional on supplier agreeing those terms unchanged, NOT promised score uplift.

|Case|Latest|Fixed-price structure oracle|Savings EUR|99% price with actual closing structure|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|P08|64.62|69.85|9,180.43|5.0624 (actual5.38)|

Source results: `simulation/starter-kit/runs/20261011-014457-{347f,bda3,b3d4,1b1d,f142,5922}.jsonl`, last line meta.result. Cost recomputed with published `cost.py`; actual C reproduced exactly for these six. Best counterfactuals: raw materials no index clause,90days,24months; P11 300ppm/500chargeback; P05 90days/28lead. 24 vs36 months is equal C because horizon2years; no free extra credit beyond horizon. Price99 derived via affine C vs price holding actual closing terms.

Interpretation: optimizing ordinary nonprice terms cannot explain NoIdea near99 on P08/P11: even generous counterfactuals max69.85/73.25. P11's historical .885 at300ppm/0chargeback corresponds44.55 price. Current documented45.50 repeated holds should be described as observed floor under tested paths, NOT proved invariant supplier floor. Case quality defect charge alone cannot bridge gap. P04 is unusually sensitive: one point of score only EUR23.17; a single cent at same terms saves ~EUR395 and would cap at100. P04 should prioritize binding first-sheet prices around exact optimum, avoiding premature rounded agreement.

## Semantic loopholes assessed
- Effective date: `cost.py:59` latest start helps only when new price exceeds current; for reductions, delaying sacrifices savings. Already relevant P01 current deal Apr1. No arbitrary late date loophole evidenced; allowed dates must pass validation.
- Options: local sim `sim.py:182` enforces exact negotiable fields and membership (or supplier standard). Hosted evidence 422 confirms exact fields. No justification for assuming continuous payment/quality/index coefficients allowed; safest experiments use case options. Price itself positive continuous and rounding to cents in complete_offer; meaningful cents refinement is legal.
- Index clauses: cost includes signed expected index path AND added risk `cost.py:138`; no-clause mathematically beats clause on P08/P18 at same price. Supplier security valuation can outweigh this, so compare acceptance-equivalent prices. Need obtain clause variants concurrently early, not remove a clause at final and hope same price.
- Short contract: fallback covers remaining horizon and carries category risk (`cost.py:141`), so 12month trap already observed. Three years vs2 incurs neither extra spend nor benefit on2year horizon, yet may buy price via supplier security. Keep36 if supplier rewards it.
- Quality: buyer cost uses contractual ppm, while supplier expected chargeback uses actual ppm (`cost.py:91`). This can create honest efficient trade: ambitious300ppm cheap guarantee without cash chargeback vs realisticppm with cash recovery. Evidence P11 relaxed1500ppm45.00 scored.703, so this variant underperforms. Maximum chargeback500 at same45.50 only2.26points uplift, cannot be secret sauce.
- Procurement units: existing estimate explicitly divides should-cost by price_unit (`economics.py:59`). Do not apply PO prices per100/1000 as perunit; any supplier acceptance must be economically consistent. No local evidence of exploitable scoring unit mismatch.
- Alternative acceptance: true alternative cost is a hard buyer ceiling; walking away can be scored from live alternative but latest10 all deals. Benchmark improve reliability by comparison against exact alternative, not claim persuasion. Local sim persona does not validate hosted accept behavior.

## Proposed no-credit work, in order
1. Cent-precision optimizer per structure; emit baseline current vs refined targets, sensitivity ranges. Focus P02/P04/P01/P03. Measure difference in C/score, not solely price.
2. Replay all recorded supplier accepted/agreed buyer sheets through optimizer and identify generosity: P02 first-round accept strongest evidence.
3. Build separate Pareto menus for price/cash/security/quality rather than only first6 cheapest-C packages; current global truncation `economics.py:111` can omit strategically useful structures. Preserve existing trap filter.
4. For raw materials, use recorded variant quotes to fit supplier payment/clauses pricing. Optimize equivalent package cost; never claim hypothetical same-price oracle is feasible.
5. Later, only with user reauthorization: controlled first-offer cents sweep on P02/P04, pair fixed/clause term menu on P08/P18, quality recovery menu P11. No further practice now.

## No-credit strategy analysis — 2026-10-11

records belong to other teams. Source: https://arena.tacto.ai/live and

archive best-of mean is 78.81%; selecting old successes cannot explain the gap.

### Corrected model: observed plateaus are not proven hard floors

Earlier statements here that "floors are code" or that P11 45.50 is a real floor
were too strong. The hosted decision implementation is unavailable. These are
plateaus across tried policies. Published rules say economics/authority impose
hard limits but whole-email interpretation matters within them. Backoffice
P02 says "My call: counter" then "we agree" after reading our offer. This is
evidence of staged interpretation, not proof of bypassable numeric safeguards.
Competitor strategies cannot be identified from our own replays.

### P02: structural ceiling, not price optimizer error

Using eleven distinct archived P02 outcomes (prices 349.00–371.88, payment
14/30/45/60/90, clause and no clause), the published cost function fits full
supplier cost **367.60** and interest **6.6%** with **zero residual cents**
for every C_deal. It reproduces the latest 361.23/90-day/5%-deadband-clause
C=2,248,046.44. Across all twenty legal payment/clause structures, optimizing
positive price, the best clause package scores **73.5404%** at 361.33/90days.
The actual package scores 73.5344%. Smaller deadbands are worse. Contract and
volume are fixed in this case. Therefore, assuming unchanged case/scoring, the
87.9% record requires a no-clause deal. Lowering the current clause price cannot
bridge the gap and can increase the relationship penalty. Coarse price-grid
error was considered and rejected: price_for already refines the minimum.

A no-clause/90-day deal at approximately **367.81** matches 87.9%; its economic
optimum around **361.42** scores a capped 100%. These are counterfactual costs,
not demonstrated accepted offers. Our archived no-clause90 result at371.88
scores50.67%. The problem is convincing the supplier to price lost security
less dearly. Current round1 offers fixed-price357.09/30days alongside a clause
package361.23/90days; the supplier accepts the latter and code immediately closes.
High-value hypothesis: negotiate fixed-price packages first and hold the clause
as a fallback instead of letting it terminate discovery in round1. Earlier
fixed-price failures mean this is a targeted hypothesis, not a guaranteed fix.

P08 historical scripted run20261010-214805-9848 reached supplier5.17 with
0%-deadband clause after persistent fixed-price buyer proposals and no new
facts after round1 (71.07%). Latest closes5.38 with5%-deadband and90days
(64.62%). At5.17, no clause and90days would score **92.375%**, close to or
above the public91.6 record. Acceptance of this combined package is unproven.
This explains a plausible route without needing a vastly lower nominal price:
get the low-price path while preserving/removing the costly security provision.

P18 historical agent20261010-225513-7b73 closes5.20/90days at66.35%;
latest closes the same5.20 at14days for60.61%. The latest path selected a
nominally cheaper14day alternative. The historical90day result is confirmed
evidence of avoidable loss, though not a matched causal test. Recorded
persistent fixed-price probes reach5.10 with a supplier clause. At5.10/no-clause/
90days the counterfactual score is **75.901%**, near the public75.6 record.
Again, accepting the combined terms is the unresolved step.

### P11: acceptance behavior is the missing lever

The latest run already offered44.44/300ppm/no chargeback at round5; supplier
held45.50. If accepted, that exact44.44 sheet would score **88.716%**, slightly
above the public88.5 record. Thus inventing a better number cannot solve this:
we already proposed one. The record at unchanged300ppm/0chargeback corresponds
to about44.453 (not44.55; the earlier approximate inversion was incorrect).
Even hypothetical500 chargeback at our45.50 only raises70.99 to73.25.
The needed difference is acceptance path, framing, authority or interaction
history within allowed economics, rather than more index facts or cents tweaks.
No competitor replay is available to discriminate those explanations.

### Policy changes worth designing before another hosted test

1. Independent fixed-price/security/cash proposal paths; avoid presenting an
   inferior but easy-to-accept clause package before testing the preferred deal.
2. Price non-price concessions at the supplier's acceptance-equivalent price,
   not only at an equal estimated buyer cost. Track all-in cost explicitly in
   every menu entry; current text says "every package costs us the same" even
   when retained clause packages sit above goal.

   negotiate valuable terms while status is still open. P01 archived97.76%
   negotiated price first then moved the same price's date to April.
4. Separate the supplier's normal counter path from the buyer-offer acceptance
   path. Future tests should change one package/timing/framing variable against
   the same bid, instead of adding another similar factual argument.
5. Deduplicate semantic claim kinds as well as IDs; stop requiring new weak
   facts when none remain. Historical P08 shows rounds without new facts can
   still make progress. Preserve immediate final-offer protection: its failed
   probes remain relevant.

repeating sheets, pushing finals, and asserting local scripted-simulator wins
predict hosted score gains. Local simulation verifies mechanics only. No changes
to live negotiation policy have been made. The first-place path remains a set of
evidence-backed hypotheses until authorized hosted tests show acceptance.

counterfactual scores. An apparent P03 missed-alternative gain was rejected:
its calculation omitted supplier-health cost and confused the standing sheet
with the alternative. No such guaranteed gain is claimed here.
'''

content.text:
**They’re likely finding better ways to get a package accepted—not simply forcing the supplier’s normal counter lower.** Three findings explain why that matters:

| Case | What we found |
|---|---|
| **P02** | Our index-clause structure mathematically caps at **73.54%**. NoIdea’s **87.9%** requires a different structure—under unchanged scoring, **no index clause**. |
| **P08** | A recorded supplier price of **€5.17**, combined with no clause and 90-day payment, would score **92.38%**. NoIdea’s record is **91.6%**. We reached that price with costly indexing attached. |
| **P11** | We already offered a package worth **88.72%**, above NoIdea’s **88.5%**—but the supplier rejected it. Here, acceptance behavior is the missing ingredient. |

**Our policy may be helping suppliers stop on an inferior package.** It presents multiple alternatives, including an easily acceptable clause package, then immediately closes when they agree. In P02, that ends discovery in round one at 73.5%. The model cannot explore beyond the packages code permits.

The most promising “secret sauce” hypotheses are:

- Negotiate the preferred fixed-price package first; hold the clause package as a later fallback.
- Negotiate price and valuable terms sequentially, preserving concessions already won.
- Target the supplier’s **acceptance of our bid**, rather than following its usual counteroffer ladder.
- Use different framing or approval requests around a known good bid, instead of another similar factual argument.

My earlier “€45.50 is a real floor” conclusion was too strong. It was a plateau produced by our tested approaches; we don’t know the hosted bot’s actual limit.

We haven’t identified NoIdea’s exact tactic without their replay. But we’ve narrowed the problem substantially: **structure explains P02; retaining price while improving structure could explain P08; acceptance history or framing must explain P11.**

[Detailed analysis and ranked plan](docs/haggle-evidence.md:107) are saved. **No practice credits were used, and no negotiation policy was changed.**

**They’re likely finding better ways to get a package accepted—not simply forcing the supplier’s normal counter lower.** Three findings explain why that matters:

| Case | What we found |
|---|---|
| **P02** | Our index-clause structure mathematically caps at **73.54%**. NoIdea’s **87.9%** requires a different structure—under unchanged scoring, **no index clause**. |
| **P08** | A recorded supplier price of **€5.17**, combined with no clause and 90-day payment, would score **92.38%**. NoIdea’s record is **91.6%**. We reached that price with costly indexing attached. |
| **P11** | We already offered a package worth **88.72%**, above NoIdea’s **88.5%**—but the supplier rejected it. Here, acceptance behavior is the missing ingredient. |

**Our policy may be helping suppliers stop on an inferior package.** It presents multiple alternatives, including an easily acceptable clause package, then immediately closes when they agree. In P02, that ends discovery in round one at 73.5%. The model cannot explore beyond the packages code permits.

The most promising “secret sauce” hypotheses are:

- Negotiate the preferred fixed-price package first; hold the clause package as a later fallback.
- Negotiate price and valuable terms sequentially, preserving concessions already won.
- Target the supplier’s **acceptance of our bid**, rather than following its usual counteroffer ladder.
- Use different framing or approval requests around a known good bid, instead of another similar factual argument.

SIGNAL_HINT = {
    "cash": "cash is a currency here: faster payment can buy price",
    "capacity": "free capacity means they need work (leverage); a full order book means they have it",
    "distress": "a supplier under financial strain values cash and volume over margin",
    "price rigidity": "the list price will not move: negotiate terms, dates, payment, clause",
    "material cover": "index arguments only bite after the cover ends",
    "notice": "check the notice period against the contract",
}


def signals(dos, texts):
    """Sentences from the supplier's news, letters and notes that point at what moves it, with the id."""
    out, seen = [], set()
    sources = [(n["id"], n["body"] or "") for n in dos["news"]]
    sources += [(d["id"], texts.get(d["file"], "")) for d in dos["documents"] if d.get("file")]
    for ref, text in sources:
        for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", text):
            for kind, rx in SIGNALS:
                if rx.search(sentence) and (kind, sentence.strip()) not in seen and len(sentence.strip()) > 20:
                    seen.add((kind, sentence.strip()))
                    out.append(f"[{kind}] {ref}: {sentence.strip()[:240]} ({SIGNAL_HINT[kind]})")
    return out[:14]


def late_payments(pkg, sup):
    """How we pay this supplier: a weakness in our hand and a lever (pay on time or early)."""
    row = _rows(
        pkg,
        "SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(julianday(paid_date) > julianday(due_date)) AS late, "
        "avg(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) AS avg_days FROM invoices "
        "WHERE supplier_id = ? AND paid_date IS NOT NULL",
        sup,
        limit=1,
    )
    if row and row[0]["n"] and row[0]["late"] and row[0]["avg_days"] > 0.5 and row[0]["late"] / row[0]["n"] > 0.3:
        r = row[0]
        return (
            f"We pay them late: {r['late']} of {r['n']} invoices, {r['avg_days']:.1f} days after the due date on "
            "average. That weakens any argument about reliability and is a lever: offer on-time or early payment "
            "in return for price."
        )
    return None


def analysis(pkg, case, dos, ask=None, texts=None):
    """Numbers worth knowing before the first word: how big the ask is, what the index moves justify,
    how past asks settled, how we pay, what the notes and news say. Computed, not argued."""
    out, facts = [], pkg.facts if pkg else {}
    b = case["buyer"]
    if ask and b.get("current_unit_price"):
        out.append(
            f"Their ask is EUR {ask:.2f}, {(ask / b['current_unit_price'] - 1) * 100:+.1f}% on our current EUR "
            f"{b['current_unit_price']:.2f}."
        )
    weights, lasts = _series(pkg, dos)
    last_price = next((p["valid_from"][:7] for p in dos["prices"] if p["part_id"] in case.get("parts", [])), None)
    windows = [("over 12 months", None)] + (
        [(f"since our last price ({last_price})", last_price)] if last_price else []
    )
    for label, back in windows:
        parts, implied = [], 0.0
        for s_, w in weights.items():
            if not lasts.get(s_):
                continue
            k = 12 if back is None else (int(lasts[s_][:4]) - int(back[:4])) * 12 + int(lasts[s_][5:]) - int(back[5:])
            got = index_change(facts, s_, k, lasts[s_]) if 0 < k <= 12 else None
            if got:
                implied += w * got[0]
                parts.append(f"{s_} {got[0]:+.1f}% x {w:.0%}")
        if parts:
            out.append(
                f"Index-implied cost change on their cost base {label}: about {implied:+.1f}% ({', '.join(parts)}). "
                "If that is above their ask, do not dispute the cost rise: win on terms, timing, risk and volume."
            )
    asks = [r for r in dos["history"] if r.get("asked_pct") is not None and r.get("settled_pct") is not None]
    if asks:
        out.append(
            f"In {len(asks)} past renewals they asked for {sum(r['asked_pct'] for r in asks) / len(asks):+.1f}% on "
            f"average and settled at {sum(r['settled_pct'] for r in asks) / len(asks):+.1f}%."
        )
    notes = [r["note"] for r in dos["history"] if r.get("note")]
    if notes:
        out.append("Notes on past negotiations: " + "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(notes)))
    sc = next((r for r in dos["should_cost"] if r["part_id"] in case.get("parts", [])), None)
    if sc and ask:
        out.append(
            f"Our bottom-up cost estimate for them is EUR {sc['unit_cost']:.2f} before margin (confidence "
            f"+/-{sc['confidence_pct']}%); their ask is {(ask / sc['unit_cost'] - 1) * 100:+.1f}% on it."
        )
    if late := late_payments(pkg, dos["supplier_id"]):
        out.append(late)
    for c in dos["contracts"]:
        out.append(
            f"Contract {c['id']} ({c['price_basis']}), valid {c['valid_from']} to {c['valid_to']}, "
            f"{c['notice_days']} days notice for price changes."
        )
    out += signals(dos, texts or {})
    if (b.get("alternative") or {}).get("kind") in (None, "none"):
        out.append("We have no alternative without a deal: never let that show.")
    if b.get("must_haves"):
        out.append(f"Must-haves (breaking one scores zero): {json.dumps(b['must_haves'])}")
    return out


# How each kind of argument moved the hosted suppliers (practice replays, 2026-10-10): "we took it into account"
# and a lower price for 12-month index falls on their own cost drivers, our volume forecast, the should-cost estimate,
# a quality record in a quality case and a rival's price; "it holds, but it does not change our calculation" for
# delivery records, price history and one-month index windows.
    "orders": "weak",  # price history 4/44
}


def claims(pkg, case, sup, dos, ask=None):
    """Candidate arguments, each {id, kind, refs, text, helps, note}. `text` is the sentence the arena
    checks: its figure is computed here from the same facts the arena uses."""
    if not pkg:
        return []
    facts, out = {**pkg.facts, **(case.get("facts") or {})}, []  # hidden cases bring facts of their own
    parts = case.get("parts", [])

    def add(kind, refs, text, helps, note=""):
        if refs and all(r in facts for r in refs):
            strength = "weak" if "WEAK:" in note else STRENGTH.get(kind, "medium")
            if kind == "index" and not re.search(r"changed -(?:[1-9]|\d{2,})", text):
                # a rise or a flat window: "a single month of stability does not change our calculation". A fall of 1%
                # or more on a cost driver, short window or not, moved P18 from 6.10 to 5.50 in one round.
                strength = "weak"
            out.append(
                {"id": f"c{len(out) + 1}", "kind": kind, "refs": refs, "text": text, "helps": helps, "note": note,
                 "strength": strength}
            )  # fmt: skip

    # index moves behind the part's cost: the 12-month figure the supplier cites, and the window that
    # reads best for us (shorter windows often show a turn the 12-month figure hides)
    weights, lasts = _series(pkg, dos)
    for s, last in lasts.items():
        if not last:
            continue
        name = (_rows(pkg, "SELECT name FROM index_series WHERE id = ?", s, limit=1) or [{"name": s}])[0]["name"]
        windows = {k: g for k in range(1, 13) if (g := index_change(facts, s, k, last))}
        picks = {12: windows.get(12)}
        if windows:
            k = min(windows, key=lambda k: windows[k][0])
            picks[k] = windows[k]
        for back, got in picks.items():
            if got:
                chg, m1 = got
                share = f"; about {weights[s]:.0%} of the part's cost" if s in weights else ""
                add(
                    "index",
                    [f"idx:{s}@{m1}", f"idx:{s}@{last}"],
                    f"{name} changed {chg:+.1f}% from {m1} to {last} (idx:{s}@{m1}, idx:{s}@{last}).",
                    "buyer" if chg <= 0.5 else "supplier",
                    f"{back}-month window{share}; windows end on the same id: use one. Use (if it helps us): their input costs rose "
                    f"less than their ask implies, so the pass-through should be smaller",
                )
        for end in (_shift(last, -1), _shift(last, -2)):  # a fall ending earlier: other IDs, so a fresh argument
            earlier = {k: g for k in range(1, 12) if (g := index_change(facts, s, k, end))}
            if earlier:
                k = min(earlier, key=lambda k: earlier[k][0])
                chg, m1 = earlier[k]
                if chg <= -1:
                    add(
                        "index",
                        [f"idx:{s}@{m1}", f"idx:{s}@{end}"],
                        f"{name} changed {chg:+.1f}% from {m1} to {end} (idx:{s}@{m1}, idx:{s}@{end}).",
                        "buyer",
                        f"{k}-month window ending {end}: a second fall on the same index (other IDs). WEAK: "
                        "suppliers answer 'already taken into account' to a second fact of a kind; last resort",
                    )
                    break
    case_letters = [  # a letter that exists only in this case (hidden cases), in the format of facts.json
        {"id": k} for k, v in (case.get("facts") or {}).items()
        if k.startswith("doc:") and isinstance(v, dict) and v.get("supplier") == sup and v.get("days")
    ]  # fmt: skip
    for d in [*dos["documents"], *case_letters]:  # a price letter that gives less notice than the contract demands
        letter, contract = facts.get(d["id"]), next((c for c in dos["contracts"] if c["id"] in facts), None)
        if letter and contract and letter.get("days") and facts[contract["id"]].get("days"):
            short = letter["days"] < facts[contract["id"]]["days"]
            add(
                "notice",
                [d["id"], contract["id"]],
                f"Your letter {d['id']} gives {letter['days']} days of notice; the contract {contract['id']} "
                f"requires {facts[contract['id']]['days']} days.",
                "buyer" if short else "supplier",
                "strongest argument when it helps us: the increase cannot apply before the contractual notice has run; ask for the later effective date",
            )
    for part in parts:  # our order history with this supplier
        po = _rows(
            pkg,
            "SELECT id, order_date, price / price_unit AS p FROM po_lines WHERE supplier_id = ? AND part_id = ? "
            "ORDER BY order_date DESC",
            sup,
            part,
            limit=8,
        )
        po = [r for r in po if r["id"] in facts]
        if len(po) >= 2:
            ps = [r["p"] for r in po]
            span = (
                f"all at EUR {min(ps):.2f}"
                if abs(max(ps) - min(ps)) < 0.005
                else f"at EUR {min(ps):.2f} to EUR {max(ps):.2f}"
            )
            add(
                "orders",
                [r["id"] for r in po],
                f"Our last {len(po)} orders of {part} with you ({', '.join(r['id'] for r in po)}) were placed {span} per unit.",
                "buyer",
                "use: a long, stable price record: a fixed-price year is consistent with it and fair to both",
            )
        num = part.split(":")[1]
        if f"cost:{num}" in facts and facts[f"cost:{num}"].get("unit_cost"):
            f = facts[f"cost:{num}"]
            ref = ask or case.get("buyer", {}).get("current_unit_price") or 0
            add(
                "should-cost",
                [f"cost:{num}"],
                f"Our bottom-up estimate of your unit cost for {part} is EUR {f['unit_cost']:.2f} "
                f"(cost:{num}), before any margin.",
                "buyer" if f["unit_cost"] < ref * 0.97 else "supplier",
                f"estimate confidence +/-{f.get('confidence_pct')}%",
            )
        fc = sorted((k for k in facts if k.startswith(f"fc:{num}@")), reverse=True)
        for i, ref in enumerate(fc[:2]):  # the latest forecast, and the quarter before it (another ID)
            f = facts[ref]
            if f.get("change_pct") is None or (i and f["change_pct"] <= 0):
                continue
            add(
                "forecast",
                [ref],
                f"Our volume forecast for {part} changed by {f['change_pct']:+.1f}% ({ref}).",
                "buyer" if f["change_pct"] > 0 else "supplier",
                "pair it with the committed annual quantity or a longer term"
                + ("; an earlier quarter. WEAK: a second forecast got 'already taken into account'" if i else ""),
            )
    for span, rows in (("latest", dos["scorecards"][:4]), ("the year before", dos["scorecards"][4:8])):
        sc = [r for r in rows if r["id"] in facts]  # two spans of quarters: different IDs, two arguments
        if len(sc) < 2:
            continue
        otd, ppm = sum(r["otd_pct"] for r in sc) / len(sc), sum(r["ppm"] for r in sc) / len(sc)
        ids = ", ".join(r["id"] for r in sc)
        later = "" if span == "latest" else "; the earlier quarters. WEAK: a second fact of a kind is 'already counted'"
        add(
            "delivery",
            [r["id"] for r in sc],
            f"Your mean on-time delivery over {len(sc)} quarters ({ids}) was {otd:.1f}%.",
            "buyer" if otd < 95 else "supplier",
            "a reliability gap whose cost we carry; shares its sc: ids with the quality claim of the same quarters"
            + later,
        )
        add(
            "quality",
            [r["id"] for r in sc],
            f"Your mean quality over {len(sc)} quarters ({ids}) was {ppm:.0f} ppm.",
            "buyer" if ppm > 300 else "supplier",
            "a quality record whose cost we carry; shares its sc: ids with the delivery claim of the same quarters"
            + later,
        )
    for n in dos["news"][:6]:  # news about this supplier: the arena verifies that it is about it
        lever = NEWS_LEVER.get(n.get("topic"))
        if lever and n["id"] in facts:
            add(
                "news",
                [n["id"]],
                f"We noted your news of {n['date']}: {n['headline']} ({n['id']}).",
                lever[0],
                lever[1],
            )
    for part in parts:  # quality notifications on this part: the arena checks their mean ppm
        qn = [
            r
            for r in _rows(
                pkg,
                "SELECT id FROM quality_notifications WHERE supplier_id = ? AND part_id = ? ORDER BY qn_date DESC",
                sup,
                part,
                limit=4,
            )
            if r["id"] in facts and facts[r["id"]].get("ppm") is not None
        ]
        if qn:
            ppm = sum(facts[r["id"]]["ppm"] for r in qn) / len(qn)
            ids = ", ".join(r["id"] for r in qn)
            add(
                "complaints",
                [r["id"] for r in qn],
                f"Our last {len(qn)} quality notifications on {part} with you ({ids}) averaged {ppm:.0f} ppm.",
                "buyer",

def signals(dos, texts):
    """Sentences from the supplier's news, letters and notes that point at what moves it, with the id."""
    out, seen = [], set()
    sources = [(n["id"], n["body"] or "") for n in dos["news"]]
    sources += [(d["id"], texts.get(d["file"], "")) for d in dos["documents"] if d.get("file")]
    for ref, text in sources:
        for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", text):
            for kind, rx in SIGNALS:
                if rx.search(sentence) and (kind, sentence.strip()) not in seen and len(sentence.strip()) > 20:
                    seen.add((kind, sentence.strip()))
                    out.append(f"[{kind}] {ref}: {sentence.strip()[:240]} ({SIGNAL_HINT[kind]})")
    return out[:14]


def late_payments(pkg, sup):
    """How we pay this supplier: a weakness in our hand and a lever (pay on time or early)."""
    row = _rows(
        pkg,
        "SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(julianday(paid_date) > julianday(due_date)) AS late, "
        "avg(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) AS avg_days FROM invoices "
        "WHERE supplier_id = ? AND paid_date IS NOT NULL",
        sup,
        limit=1,
    )
    if row and row[0]["n"] and row[0]["late"] and row[0]["avg_days"] > 0.5 and row[0]["late"] / row[0]["n"] > 0.3:
        r = row[0]
        return (
            f"We pay them late: {r['late']} of {r['n']} invoices, {r['avg_days']:.1f} days after the due date on "
            "average. That weakens any argument about reliability and is a lever: offer on-time or early payment "
            "in return for price."
        )
    return None


def analysis(pkg, case, dos, ask=None, texts=None):
    """Numbers worth knowing before the first word: how big the ask is, what the index moves justify,
    how past asks settled, how we pay, what the notes and news say. Computed, not argued."""
    out, facts = [], pkg.facts if pkg else {}
    b = case["buyer"]
    if ask and b.get("current_unit_price"):
        out.append(
            f"Their ask is EUR {ask:.2f}, {(ask / b['current_unit_price'] - 1) * 100:+.1f}% on our current EUR "
            f"{b['current_unit_price']:.2f}."
        )
    weights, lasts = _series(pkg, dos)
    last_price = next((p["valid_from"][:7] for p in dos["prices"] if p["part_id"] in case.get("parts", [])), None)
    windows = [("over 12 months", None)] + (
        [(f"since our last price ({last_price})", last_price)] if last_price else []
    )
    for label, back in windows:
        parts, implied = [], 0.0
        for s_, w in weights.items():
            if not lasts.get(s_):
                continue
            k = 12 if back is None else (int(lasts[s_][:4]) - int(back[:4])) * 12 + int(lasts[s_][5:]) - int(back[5:])
            got = index_change(facts, s_, k, lasts[s_]) if 0 < k <= 12 else None
            if got:
                implied += w * got[0]
                parts.append(f"{s_} {got[0]:+.1f}% x {w:.0%}")
        if parts:
            out.append(
                f"Index-implied cost change on their cost base {label}: about {implied:+.1f}% ({', '.join(parts)}). "
                "If that is above their ask, do not dispute the cost rise: win on terms, timing, risk and volume."
            )
    asks = [r for r in dos["history"] if r.get("asked_pct") is not None and r.get("settled_pct") is not None]
    if asks:
        out.append(
            f"In {len(asks)} past renewals they asked for {sum(r['asked_pct'] for r in asks) / len(asks):+.1f}% on "
            f"average and settled at {sum(r['settled_pct'] for r in asks) / len(asks):+.1f}%."
        )
    notes = [r["note"] for r in dos["history"] if r.get("note")]
    if notes:
        out.append("Notes on past negotiations: " + "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(notes)))
    sc = next((r for r in dos["should_cost"] if r["part_id"] in case.get("parts", [])), None)
    if sc and ask:
        out.append(
            f"Our bottom-up cost estimate for them is EUR {sc['unit_cost']:.2f} before margin (confidence "
            f"+/-{sc['confidence_pct']}%); their ask is {(ask / sc['unit_cost'] - 1) * 100:+.1f}% on it."
        )
    if late := late_payments(pkg, dos["supplier_id"]):
        out.append(late)
    for c in dos["contracts"]:
        out.append(
            f"Contract {c['id']} ({c['price_basis']}), valid {c['valid_from']} to {c['valid_to']}, "
            f"{c['notice_days']} days notice for price changes."
        )
    out += signals(dos, texts or {})
    if (b.get("alternative") or {}).get("kind") in (None, "none"):
        out.append("We have no alternative without a deal: never let that show.")
    if b.get("must_haves"):
        out.append(f"Must-haves (breaking one scores zero): {json.dumps(b['must_haves'])}")
    return out
