# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

"""What a term sheet really costs us, and what the best sheet probably is.

The score is C, not the unit price. C also charges payment interest, the risk of an index clause and, in
`stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, a penalty for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a
sustainable margin. That penalty needs the supplier's full cost, which we estimate from the should-cost row
(`method: bottom-up estimate, no margin`, confidence about +/-5%). With it the agent can see that, in such a
case, a lower price can raise C, and can search the allowed options for the cheapest sheet."""

import itertools

from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, closing_terms, complete_offer, must_haves_ok, supplier_value, total_cost

# Without a cost estimate, plan down to this share of the supplier's price: the best package a supplier accepted
# sat at 84-87% of its opening price in the hosted cases without a supplier-health charge (P05, P08, P10).
NO_ESTIMATE_FLOOR = 0.85
FLOOR_MARGIN = -3.0  # outside relationship cases: the lowest supplier margin (%) we plan to ask for


ASK_MARGIN = 0.99  # a supplier does not ask for less than about its cost: full cost <= 99% of its own ask
# Calibrated on settled hosted sessions (P01 twice, P02 twice): the arena's exact cost breakdown implies a full
# cost of 0.98 x the should-cost estimate every time (129.95 vs 132.64, 130.04 vs 132.64, 367.6 vs 374.95,
# 367.8 vs 374.95), so the estimate runs about 2% high.
SHOULD_COST_BIAS = 0.98
# What money is worth to a supplier until its own sheets show it (`Negotiator.learn_money`): one point under our
# rate (Nordmark priced payment days at about 7% a year against our 8%). At our own rate every payment term looks
# equal to us in a supplier-health case and the menu took 45 days; at the supplier's lower rate the longest term
# is cheaper for us (P02: 361.50 at 90 days with the clause, agreed in round 1, 0.735 against 0.659 at 45 days).
# A supplier under financial strain keeps our rate: cash is dearer to it.
SUPPLIER_RATE_DISCOUNT = 0.01
STRAIN_TOPICS = {"restructuring", "credit_downgrade", "credit_watch", "short_time_work"}


def full_standard(dos, pdf_standard):
    """The supplier's standard terms: its master record (payment days, Incoterm, lead time) overlaid with what
    its quote PDF states (quality commitment, chargeback). The PDF alone omits the cash terms that
    `supplier_value` needs."""
    master = dos.get("master") or {}
    base = {
        "payment_days": master.get("payment_days"),
        "incoterm": master.get("incoterm"),
        "lead_time_days": master.get("standard_lead_time_days"),
    }
    return {**{k: v for k, v in base.items() if v is not None}, **pdf_standard}


def estimate(case, dos, std, ask=None):
    """Our model of the supplier for `supplier_value`; `full_cost` only if the data has a should-cost,
    capped just under the supplier's own ask (the should-cost is only good to about +/-5%)."""
    rate = case["buyer"]["interest_rate"]
    if not any(n.get("topic") in STRAIN_TOPICS for n in dos.get("news", [])):
        rate -= SUPPLIER_RATE_DISCOUNT
    est = {"standard": std, "interest_rate": rate}
    part = (case.get("parts") or [None])[0]
    rows = [r for r in dos.get("should_cost", []) if r["part_id"] == part] or dos.get("should_cost", [])
    if rows and rows[0].get("unit_cost"):
        est["full_cost"] = SHOULD_COST_BIAS * rows[0]["unit_cost"] / (rows[0].get("price_unit") or 1)
        if ask:
            est["full_cost"] = min(est["full_cost"], ask * ASK_MARGIN)
    return est


def margin(case, terms, std, est):
    """The supplier's margin in % on this sheet, by our estimate (None without a cost estimate)."""
    if "full_cost" not in est:
        return None
    try:
        worth = supplier_value(case, closing_terms(case, terms, std), est)
    except (KeyError, TypeError):
        return None
    return (worth - est["full_cost"]) / worth * 100


def cost(case, terms, std, est):
    """C including our estimate of the supplier-health charge."""
    try:
        return total_cost(case, terms, std, est if "full_cost" in est else None)
    except (KeyError, TypeError):  # the supplier model could not read the standard terms
        return total_cost(case, terms, std)


def relationship_case(case):
    return case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS


def plan(case, std, est, price):
    """The cheapest sheet by C(est) over the allowed options and prices up to `price` (the supplier's own
    price), as {target, packages}: `target` is the best sheet, `packages` the best sheet of every option
    combination (payment days, index clause, ...), cheapest first. Outside relationship cases a sheet only
    counts if the supplier's estimated margin stays above FLOOR_MARGIN."""
    fields = [f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price"]
    options = [case.get("term_options", {}).get(f) or [None] for f in fields]
    probe = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": price})
    # No usable cost estimate (no should-cost, or terms the supplier model cannot read): plan conservatively
    known = margin(case, probe, std, est) is not None
    deepest = round((1 - NO_ESTIMATE_FLOOR) * 100)  # with or without an estimate: P10 refused 80%, took 87%
    best = {}
    for combo in itertools.product(*options):
        base = dict(zip(fields, combo, strict=True))
        for k in range(0, deepest + 1):
            sheet = complete_offer(case, {**base, "unit_price": round(price * (1 - k / 100), 2)})
            if not must_haves_ok(case, sheet, std):
                continue
            m = margin(case, sheet, std, est)
            if k > 0 and not relationship_case(case) and m is not None and m < FLOOR_MARGIN:
                break
            c = cost(case, sheet, std, est if known else {})
            key = repr(base)
            if key not in best or c < best[key]["c"]:
                best[key] = {"terms": sheet, "c": c, "margin": None if m is None else round(m, 2)}
    packages = sorted(best.values(), key=lambda p: p["c"])
    return {"target": packages[0] if packages else None, "packages": packages[:6], "modelled": known}


def levers(case, std, est, terms):
    """What each lever costs us (EUR of C) against the supplier's own sheet `terms`, one lever at a time, plus
    1% on the price. A lever the supplier values and that costs us little is worth testing: it can buy price."""
    base = cost(case, terms, std, est)
    volume = case["buyer"]["need_per_year"] * case["buyer"]["horizon_years"]
    out = [
        {
            "lever": "unit_price -1%",
            "delta_c": round(
                cost(case, {**terms, "unit_price": round(terms["unit_price"] * 0.99, 2)}, std, est) - base
            ),
        }
    ]
    for field in (f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price"):
        for value in case.get("term_options", {}).get(field) or []:
            if value != terms.get(field):
                t = complete_offer(case, {**terms, field: value})
                delta = cost(case, t, std, est) - base
                out.append(
                    {"lever": f"{field} = {value}", "delta_c": round(delta), "per_unit": round(delta / volume, 2)}
                )
    return out

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

"""What a term sheet really costs us, and what the best sheet probably is.

The score is C, not the unit price. C also charges payment interest, the risk of an index clause and, in
`stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, a penalty for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a
sustainable margin. That penalty needs the supplier's full cost, which we estimate from the should-cost row
(`method: bottom-up estimate, no margin`, confidence about +/-5%). With it the agent can see that, in such a
case, a lower price can raise C, and can search the allowed options for the cheapest sheet."""

import itertools

from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, closing_terms, complete_offer, must_haves_ok, supplier_value, total_cost

# Without a cost estimate, plan down to this share of the supplier's price: the best package a supplier accepted
# sat at 84-87% of its opening price in the hosted cases without a supplier-health charge (P05, P08, P10).
NO_ESTIMATE_FLOOR = 0.85
FLOOR_MARGIN = -3.0  # outside relationship cases: the lowest supplier margin (%) we plan to ask for


ASK_MARGIN = 0.99  # a supplier does not ask for less than about its cost: full cost <= 99% of its own ask
# Calibrated on settled hosted sessions (P01 twice, P02 twice): the arena's exact cost breakdown implies a full
# cost of 0.98 x the should-cost estimate every time (129.95 vs 132.64, 130.04 vs 132.64, 367.6 vs 374.95,
# 367.8 vs 374.95), so the estimate runs about 2% high.
SHOULD_COST_BIAS = 0.98
# What money is worth to a supplier until its own sheets show it (`Negotiator.learn_money`): one point under our
# rate (Nordmark priced payment days at about 7% a year against our 8%). At our own rate every payment term looks
# equal to us in a supplier-health case and the menu took 45 days; at the supplier's lower rate the longest term
# is cheaper for us (P02: 361.50 at 90 days with the clause, agreed in round 1, 0.735 against 0.659 at 45 days).
# A supplier under financial strain keeps our rate: cash is dearer to it.
SUPPLIER_RATE_DISCOUNT = 0.01
STRAIN_TOPICS = {"restructuring", "credit_downgrade", "credit_watch", "short_time_work"}


def full_standard(dos, pdf_standard):
    """The supplier's standard terms: its master record (payment days, Incoterm, lead time) overlaid with what
    its quote PDF states (quality commitment, chargeback). The PDF alone omits the cash terms that
    `supplier_value` needs."""
    master = dos.get("master") or {}
    base = {
        "payment_days": master.get("payment_days"),
        "incoterm": master.get("incoterm"),
        "lead_time_days": master.get("standard_lead_time_days"),
    }
    return {**{k: v for k, v in base.items() if v is not None}, **pdf_standard}


def estimate(case, dos, std, ask=None):
    """Our model of the supplier for `supplier_value`; `full_cost` only if the data has a should-cost,
    capped just under the supplier's own ask (the should-cost is only good to about +/-5%)."""
    rate = case["buyer"]["interest_rate"]
    if not any(n.get("topic") in STRAIN_TOPICS for n in dos.get("news", [])):
        rate -= SUPPLIER_RATE_DISCOUNT
    est = {"standard": std, "interest_rate": rate}
    part = (case.get("parts") or [None])[0]
    rows = [r for r in dos.get("should_cost", []) if r["part_id"] == part] or dos.get("should_cost", [])
    if rows and rows[0].get("unit_cost"):
        est["full_cost"] = SHOULD_COST_BIAS * rows[0]["unit_cost"] / (rows[0].get("price_unit") or 1)
        if ask:
            est["full_cost"] = min(est["full_cost"], ask * ASK_MARGIN)
    return est


def margin(case, terms, std, est):
    """The supplier's margin in % on this sheet, by our estimate (None without a cost estimate)."""
    if "full_cost" not in est:
        return None
    try:
        worth = supplier_value(case, closing_terms(case, terms, std), est)
    except (KeyError, TypeError):
        return None
    return (worth - est["full_cost"]) / worth * 100


def cost(case, terms, std, est):
    """C including our estimate of the supplier-health charge."""
    try:
        return total_cost(case, terms, std, est if "full_cost" in est else None)
    except (KeyError, TypeError):  # the supplier model could not read the standard terms
        return total_cost(case, terms, std)


def relationship_case(case):
    return case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS


def plan(case, std, est, price):
    """The cheapest sheet by C(est) over the allowed options and prices up to `price` (the supplier's own
    price), as {target, packages}: `target` is the best sheet, `packages` the best sheet of every option
    combination (payment days, index clause, ...), cheapest first. Outside relationship cases a sheet only
    counts if the supplier's estimated margin stays above FLOOR_MARGIN."""
    fields = [f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price"]
    options = [case.get("term_options", {}).get(f) or [None] for f in fields]
    probe = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": price})
    # No usable cost estimate (no should-cost, or terms the supplier model cannot read): plan conservatively
    known = margin(case, probe, std, est) is not None
    deepest = round((1 - NO_ESTIMATE_FLOOR) * 100)  # with or without an estimate: P10 refused 80%, took 87%
    best = {}
    for combo in itertools.product(*options):
        base = dict(zip(fields, combo, strict=True))
        for k in range(0, deepest + 1):
            sheet = complete_offer(case, {**base, "unit_price": round(price * (1 - k / 100), 2)})
            if not must_haves_ok(case, sheet, std):
                continue
            m = margin(case, sheet, std, est)
            if k > 0 and not relationship_case(case) and m is not None and m < FLOOR_MARGIN:
                break
            c = cost(case, sheet, std, est if known else {})
            key = repr(base)
            if key not in best or c < best[key]["c"]:
                best[key] = {"terms": sheet, "c": c, "margin": None if m is None else round(m, 2)}
    packages = sorted(best.values(), key=lambda p: p["c"])
    return {"target": packages[0] if packages else None, "packages": packages[:6], "modelled": known}


def levers(case, std, est, terms):
    """What each lever costs us (EUR of C) against the supplier's own sheet `terms`, one lever at a time, plus
    1% on the price. A lever the supplier values and that costs us little is worth testing: it can buy price."""
    base = cost(case, terms, std, est)
    volume = case["buyer"]["need_per_year"] * case["buyer"]["horizon_years"]
    out = [
        {
            "lever": "unit_price -1%",
            "delta_c": round(
                cost(case, {**terms, "unit_price": round(terms["unit_price"] * 0.99, 2)}, std, est) - base
            ),
        }
    ]
    for field in (f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price"):
        for value in case.get("term_options", {}).get(field) or []:
            if value != terms.get(field):
                t = complete_offer(case, {**terms, field: value})
                delta = cost(case, t, std, est) - base
                out.append(
                    {"lever": f"{field} = {value}", "delta_c": round(delta), "per_unit": round(delta / volume, 2)}
                )
    return out

def _fmt(v):
    return "none" if v is None else f"{v:.2f}" if isinstance(v, float) else str(v)


def pdf(title, sections):
    """A one-page PDF of text lines, labelled like the arena's quotes."""
    lines = [title]
    for head, terms in sections:
        lines += [head, *(f"{NAMES.get(k, k)} {_fmt(v)}" for k, v in terms.items())]
    esc = [x.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)") for x in lines]
    text = "".join(f"BT /F1 10 Tf 50 {800 - 14 * i} Td ({t}) Tj ET\n" for i, t in enumerate(esc))
    page = "/MediaBox [0 0 595 842] /Resources << /Font << /F1 4 0 R >> >> /Contents 5 0 R"
    objs = [
        "<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
        "<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
        f"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R {page} >>",
        "<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>",
        f"<< /Length {len(text)} >>\nstream\n{text}endstream",
    ]
    out, offsets = "%PDF-1.4\n", []
    for i, obj in enumerate(objs, 1):
        offsets.append(len(out))
        out += f"{i} 0 obj\n{obj}\nendobj\n"
    xref = f"xref\n0 {len(objs) + 1}\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
    xref += "".join(f"{o:010d} 00000 n \n" for o in offsets)
    tail = f"trailer\n<< /Size {len(objs) + 1} /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n{len(out)}\n%%EOF\n"
    return (out + xref + tail).encode("latin-1", "replace")


def xlsx(price):

    wb = Workbook()

    ws.append(["Unit price", "=SUM(B2:B5)", "=SUM(C2:C5)"])

def late_payments(pkg, sup):
    """How we pay this supplier: a weakness in our hand and a lever (pay on time or early)."""
    row = _rows(
        pkg,
        "SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(julianday(paid_date) > julianday(due_date)) AS late, "
        "avg(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) AS avg_days FROM invoices "
        "WHERE supplier_id = ? AND paid_date IS NOT NULL",
        sup,
        limit=1,
    )
    if row and row[0]["n"] and row[0]["late"] and row[0]["avg_days"] > 0.5 and row[0]["late"] / row[0]["n"] > 0.3:
        r = row[0]
        return (
            f"We pay them late: {r['late']} of {r['n']} invoices, {r['avg_days']:.1f} days after the due date on "
            "average. That weakens any argument about reliability and is a lever: offer on-time or early payment "
            "in return for price."
        )
    return None


def analysis(pkg, case, dos, ask=None, texts=None):
    """Numbers worth knowing before the first word: how big the ask is, what the index moves justify,
    how past asks settled, how we pay, what the notes and news say. Computed, not argued."""
    out, facts = [], pkg.facts if pkg else {}
    b = case["buyer"]
    if ask and b.get("current_unit_price"):
        out.append(
            f"Their ask is EUR {ask:.2f}, {(ask / b['current_unit_price'] - 1) * 100:+.1f}% on our current EUR "
            f"{b['current_unit_price']:.2f}."
        )
    weights, lasts = _series(pkg, dos)
    last_price = next((p["valid_from"][:7] for p in dos["prices"] if p["part_id"] in case.get("parts", [])), None)
    windows = [("over 12 months", None)] + (
        [(f"since our last price ({last_price})", last_price)] if last_price else []
    )
    for label, back in windows:
        parts, implied = [], 0.0
        for s_, w in weights.items():
            if not lasts.get(s_):
                continue
            k = 12 if back is None else (int(lasts[s_][:4]) - int(back[:4])) * 12 + int(lasts[s_][5:]) - int(back[5:])
            got = index_change(facts, s_, k, lasts[s_]) if 0 < k <= 12 else None
            if got:
                implied += w * got[0]
                parts.append(f"{s_} {got[0]:+.1f}% x {w:.0%}")
        if parts:
            out.append(
                f"Index-implied cost change on their cost base {label}: about {implied:+.1f}% ({', '.join(parts)}). "
                "If that is above their ask, do not dispute the cost rise: win on terms, timing, risk and volume."
            )
    asks = [r for r in dos["history"] if r.get("asked_pct") is not None and r.get("settled_pct") is not None]
    if asks:
        out.append(
            f"In {len(asks)} past renewals they asked for {sum(r['asked_pct'] for r in asks) / len(asks):+.1f}% on "
            f"average and settled at {sum(r['settled_pct'] for r in asks) / len(asks):+.1f}%."
        )
    notes = [r["note"] for r in dos["history"] if r.get("note")]
    if notes:
        out.append("Notes on past negotiations: " + "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(notes)))
    sc = next((r for r in dos["should_cost"] if r["part_id"] in case.get("parts", [])), None)
    if sc and ask:
        out.append(
            f"Our bottom-up cost estimate for them is EUR {sc['unit_cost']:.2f} before margin (confidence "
            f"+/-{sc['confidence_pct']}%); their ask is {(ask / sc['unit_cost'] - 1) * 100:+.1f}% on it."
        )
    if late := late_payments(pkg, dos["supplier_id"]):
        out.append(late)
    for c in dos["contracts"]:
        out.append(
            f"Contract {c['id']} ({c['price_basis']}), valid {c['valid_from']} to {c['valid_to']}, "
            f"{c['notice_days']} days notice for price changes."
        )
    out += signals(dos, texts or {})
    if (b.get("alternative") or {}).get("kind") in (None, "none"):
        out.append("We have no alternative without a deal: never let that show.")
    if b.get("must_haves"):
        out.append(f"Must-haves (breaking one scores zero): {json.dumps(b['must_haves'])}")
    return out

def reachable_c(case, std, est, ref_price):
    """The lowest C any allowed structure reaches at a price inside the menu's range (LOWEST_SHARE of the
    supplier's price up to its ask)."""
    best = math.inf
    for base in structures(case):
        base = {**base, **free_for_them(case, std, base)}
        if not must_haves_ok(case, complete_offer(case, {**base, "unit_price": ref_price}), std):
            continue
        lo = ref_price * LOWEST_SHARE
        for k in range(41):  # C can be U-shaped in price (supplier-health charge): scan, do not assume the bottom
            p = round(lo + (ref_price - lo) * k / 40, 2)
            best = min(best, eco.cost(case, complete_offer(case, {**base, "unit_price": p}), std, est))
    return best


def free_for_them(case, std, base):
    """Terms that cost the supplier no cash but save us money: a ppm commitment without a chargeback is a promise,
    not a payment, so it goes to the tightest allowed value (P11: 45.50 at 300 ppm and at 800 ppm alike)."""
    out = {}
    options = case.get("term_options", {})
    if "ppm_commitment" in case["negotiable"] and options.get("ppm_commitment"):
        if not base.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint"):
            out["ppm_commitment"] = min(options["ppm_commitment"])
    return out


def tags(terms, theirs, case):
    """What a package offers the supplier, in its own currency, for the model to match to what it said it values."""
    out = []
    if theirs and all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in theirs.items() if k not in ("unit_price", "ppm_commitment")):
        out.append("their structure")
    if terms.get("index_clause"):
        out.append("security: index clause")
    months = case.get("term_options", {}).get("contract_months") or []
    if months and terms.get("contract_months") == max(months):
        out.append("security: longest contract")
    volumes = case.get("term_options", {}).get("volume_per_year") or []
    if volumes and terms.get("volume_per_year") == max(volumes):
        out.append("security: most volume")
    pay = terms.get("payment_days")
    ref = theirs.get("payment_days") if theirs else None
    if pay is not None and ref is not None and pay < ref:
        out.append("cash: faster payment")
    if pay is not None and ref is not None and pay > ref:
        out.append("costs them: longer payment")
    return out or ["price"]

def late_payments(pkg, sup):
    """How we pay this supplier: a weakness in our hand and a lever (pay on time or early)."""
    row = _rows(
        pkg,
        "SELECT count(*) AS n, sum(julianday(paid_date) > julianday(due_date)) AS late, "
        "avg(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) AS avg_days FROM invoices "
        "WHERE supplier_id = ? AND paid_date IS NOT NULL",
        sup,
        limit=1,
    )
    if row and row[0]["n"] and row[0]["late"] and row[0]["avg_days"] > 0.5 and row[0]["late"] / row[0]["n"] > 0.3:

def reachable_c(case, std, est, ref_price):
    """The lowest C any allowed structure reaches at a price inside the menu's range (LOWEST_SHARE of the
    supplier's price up to its ask)."""
    best = math.inf
    for base in structures(case):
        base = {**base, **free_for_them(case, std, base)}
        if not must_haves_ok(case, complete_offer(case, {**base, "unit_price": ref_price}), std):
            continue
        lo = ref_price * LOWEST_SHARE
        for k in range(41):  # C can be U-shaped in price (supplier-health charge): scan, do not assume the bottom
            p = round(lo + (ref_price - lo) * k / 40, 2)
            best = min(best, eco.cost(case, complete_offer(case, {**base, "unit_price": p}), std, est))
    return best

    not a payment, so it goes to the tightest allowed value (P11: 45.50 at 300 ppm and at 800 ppm alike)."""

    options = case.get("term_options", {})

Payload:
Nine concrete mechanisms worth separating from fixed-price repetition:

1. **Document evidence cannot pass through the current message builder.** `agent.py:580` strips document/data IDs unless they are current offer IDs; only subsequent canned claim markers restore references. `agent.py:599–606` permits figures from selected claims, menu sheets and supplier replies, excluding original documents. """The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""

    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price

    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]

    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
"}

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > docs/haggle-breakthrough-hypotheses.md <<'EOF'
# Broader Haggle hypotheses after the failed opening screen

<!-- index: design | Broader evidence-backed hypotheses after failed opening screen | Choosing distinct negotiation mechanisms without spending practice credits. -->

Completed analysis, 2026-10-11. **No new hosted sessions or practice credits.**
No default-agent changes. The two-credit opening-only screen did not improve P02
or P08. It is insufficient evidence to reject every fixed-price route, but it is
also insufficient reason to spend another session repeating that idea.

## What this investigation changes

The most concrete new findings concern our agent's limitations, not magic
wording. There is direct evidence it skipped a fresh rival quote because its
marker looked old, and mechanical evidence that some valid source references
and figures cannot pass through its message builder. These deserve attention
before assuming the suppliers are unreachable. Competitor replays remain
unavailable; none of the ideas below identifies NoIdea's actual strategy.

The current suite averaged 77.2176%, versus the earlier public best-of snapshot
of 88.0% for NoIdea. Those measures differ. Reaching first place needs improvements
across several cases, not just P02/P08; matching the public P02/P08/P18 records
would move the suite only to about 82.85%.

## Ranked mechanisms

| Priority | Mechanism | Evidence and uncertainty | Discriminating test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Fresh rival quotes with persistent, distinct identities | P05 actually supplied new 27.50 evidence to the model, which skipped it as already used. Offline reproduction confirms alias reuse. Supplier response still unproven. | Same quotes/bids, distinct marker per offer; compare selection first offline, then a matched hosted trial. |
| 2 | Make document-backed evidence usable | Builder strips contextual document IDs and rejects a documented committee threshold absent from canned claims. Reproduced offline. | Verify allowed source references and figures reach the outgoing message; supplier acceptance is a separate trial. |
| 3 | Plan tender order around newly obtained competitor quotes | An older P05 round-4 fresh-rival attempt walked away; current round-3 message missed the quote. Earlier use remains open. | Challenger receives the verified fresh quote before its last productive round; retain timeout/final protections. |
| 4 | Independent argument families, not two superficially strong facts | P07's opening used two forecasts; the second was duplicate. Later another forecast and quality claim also duplicated. | Same package and claim count, one forecast plus a genuinely distinct relevant source; no invented family or gain. |
| 5 | Approval-ready exception request anchored in the supplier's actual procedure | P07/P10 notes name a 2% committee threshold; generic P11 boss escalation failed. | Cite the real procedure and request approval of a complete package while open; inspect backoffice for actual escalation. |
| 6 | Ask for a differential quotation before making a binding concession | Agent requires every send to select an offer; every diagnostic message can therefore end negotiation. | One precise allowed-structure quote comparison on a patient supplier; do not assume a question earns a price concession. |
| 7 | Separate acquisition of price from acquisition of terms | P01 reached 97.76% by getting price first, then April at unchanged price. | Same-price term request while open, one term at a time; do not reopen a final offer. |
| 8 | Response to a specific evidence request, with a minimal canonical export | P11 repeatedly asks for underlying figures; one mixed CSV attempt was contradicted. That does not establish all accurate evidence delivery fails. | Reconcile every exported value first; one requested record, no extra claims or altered bid; measure trust/acceptance. |
| 9 | Learn supplier security premiums instead of sorting by cash value | Published supplier_value excludes index and duration; menus price packages to one buyer C. | Matched quotes differing in exactly one allowed field, infer the premium, then offer a separately priced exchange. |
| 10 | Test presentation/selection sensitivity at identical economics | P02 backoffice moves from counter to agreement after reading the email. Selection implementation unavailable. | Swap order of identical packages or send one clear package; keep prose/claims matched; do not claim a numeric bypass. |
| 11 | A technical referral branch, gated on original-case validity | P11 offers possible 1.15 material/tolerance or 0.72 lot savings; agent declines. Specification change/approval cannot currently be encoded. | Ask which savings can apply to the approved original part and request conditional quotation; no fabricated approval. |
| 12 | Replace an already-counted quality argument with price history where appropriate | P18 staged historical run used orders, then received 5.10. Other variables differ; causality unknown. | Same package/sequence, swap only the later argument; compare against duplicate-quality control. |
| 13 | Revalue remembered quotes after updating the supplier model | Interest estimate changes but stored best numeric C is not first recomputed. Source-level concern; no measured loss yet. | Offline fixture with paired payment quotes; consistent revaluation before deciding rescue or structure. |
| 14 | Case-specific anchor/concession policies | High-opening P11 and uniformly slow ladders already failed; current policies apply broad empirical rules. | Compare a new path only for a diagnosed motive, not a universal lower-price multiplier. P10 finalizes after one message. |

## 1. P05: an updated quote is being mistaken for a spent argument

Source: `arena_kit/haggle/agent.py:269` regenerates the live rival claim using
`r1` every time. Claim eligibility correctly distinguishes the underlying offer
IDs, but the conversation keeps the old marker and says never to repeat a claim.

In `runs/20261011-014457-f142.jsonl:25`, Claudia's third model request explicitly
includes the unused strong claim `r1`, price 27.50, reference `offer:70210-2`.
The response nevertheless says **“the rival marker has already been used”** and
chooses delivery evidence. Earlier `r1` described 31.50, then 30.50. Those are
three different live supplier offers, not repeated assertions of one quote.
The subsequent leader final ends the tender before this opportunity is explored.

Offline reproduction using the real Negotiator confirmed two distinct unused
references receive the same marker. This proves alias reuse and shows a specific
model misinterpretation; it does not prove an extra supplier concession.

Candidate: a stable marker identity per actual offer plus explicit “new offer
superseding the previously cited quote” language. Tell the challenger the latest
valid comparable offer before sending the leader a likely terminal price request.
Do not fabricate a rival or quote a lapsed/noncomparable offer. Under the current
serialized arena gate, delaying a leader can cause a timeout; coordinating this
requires a deadline-aware schedule, not simply waiting for another reply.

Counterevidence: `20261010-211528-331a.jsonl:30` sent the real 27.50 quote to
Claudia at round 4; she walked away. New identities alone cannot restore patience
already lost. Early use and scheduling are a separate experiment from alias repair.

## 2. Evidence bottleneck: the model cannot use everything it reads

`agent.py:580` removes IDs not present in current supplier/rival offers, then
restores selected canned claim markers. Its numeric validator at `:599` admits
selected claim figures, menu figures and supplier reply figures; original source
documents are absent. Outgoing messages at `:618` have no refs/attachments path.
This is protective validation with an incomplete evidence catalogue.

Offline reproduction: the source ID `doc:20260513-70610-M1` was stripped from a
truthful committee request. Its documented 2% threshold was rejected as an
unverified figure when absent from the offer/supplier-reply corpus. The source
is `data/correspondence/20260513-70610-M1.md:5`; P10 has the same stated procedure
in `20260310-70410-M1.md:5`.

Candidate: verify a source ID exists, retain its exact relevant sentence and
provenance as a selectable claim, and permit only source-supported figures.
This could make capacity notes, price-approval procedures, reference-customer
statements and specific contractual clauses usable as evidence. Do not remove
validation or let the model invent new calculations unchecked. A truthful source
may still be irrelevant or already counted by the supplier.

For P07 specifically, the note about a second shift on hold since spring is in
`20260514-70610-M3.md:5`, but the generic news claim generator does not create a
claim from meeting/call-note capacity statements. Its current opening chose two
forecasts, one of which was duplicate. A supplier-specific capacity argument is
an independent candidate; its economic relevance and verification remain open.

## 3. Approval is a process to satisfy, not a magic phrase

P07/P10 sources specify committee approval above 2%, with fortnightly meetings.
A concrete candidate is: “Your annual review describes committee approval for
this scale of change. Please submit the complete package below, with the forecast
and capacity rationale, for the required price approval and tell us what evidence
is missing.” No claim that approval has happened, no invented meeting date.

Success requires a real recorded approval path and revised valid standing terms,
not a sales rep saying “I checked with the boss.” P11 already produced that phrase
without a corresponding approval in backoffice and kept 45.50. The new hypothesis
is a procedure-specific, evidenced exception request on the relevant suppliers.
P10's current first reply is final: any request must be in the opening, not after it.

## 4. Do not force every question to be a binding bargain

The supplier can immediately accept any offered sheet. The agent rejects model
sends without offer keys (`agent.py:571`). This restricts information discovery.
A narrow paired-quote request could ask: “At the same payment and duration, please
quote the indexed and fixed alternatives and identify the fixed-price premium.”
Another asks whether 24 months resolves the objection specific to 36 months.

A plain question alone previously produced no price on P11; it also consumes a
round and patience. Use only when the answer can change the policy materially.
For short-patience P10, this is a poor default. Never mistake a conditional quote
for an accepted package or assume an old fallback remains available.

## 5. Learn the missing supplier utility

Our numeric supplier cash-value model deliberately excludes contract duration
and index security (`cost.py:81`). The menu ranks estimated cash worth and mostly
makes alternatives equal in buyer cost (`strategy.py:109`). Thus it offers a
useful heuristic rather than a measured acceptance frontier.

A quote pair that differs only in payment, deadband or duration reveals what that
supplier charges for the term. The relevant question becomes: is the supplier's
premium below the buyer's avoided cost? Unequal packages can be useful diagnostic
probes if each is individually acceptable to close; equal-C menus are not the
only sensible design. Never bundle several changes and attribute the response
to one lever. This is a generalizable policy for unseen suppliers.

## Lower-confidence branches and what already failed

- **Technical savings:** 1.15 happens to match P11's price gap, but the engineering
  variant may invalidate the part. Clarify original-specification lot savings or
  real approval requirements before any award; current API calls variants
  informational. A cheaper altered part is not demonstrated score improvement.
- **Minimal evidence:** the earlier kitchen-sink CSV bundled scorecards, complaint
  rows and several unrelated levers, and was contradicted. Some exported values
  match facts.json on inspection; the exact failure cause is unknown. Therefore
